paragraphs.text: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome-8 (PPGL8) is an autosomal dominant tumor predisposition caused by germline TMEM127 mutations. It mainly causes catecholamine-secreting pheochromocytomas of the adrenal medulla. These tumors are often bilateral or multicentric and usually benign, and onset is at an age similar to that of sporadic pheochromocytoma (Qin et al., 2010; Yao et al., 2010; Toledo et al., 2015). Paragangliomas and renal cell carcinoma have been reported less often in carriers, but whether they are causally linked to TMEM127 mutations has not been established (Armaiz-Pena et al., 2021).

paragraphs.text: Qin et al. (2010) reported 7 index patients or families with germline TMEM127 mutations. Four had a family history of pheochromocytoma, 2 had no family history, and 1 had been adopted. On average, patients developed pheochromocytoma at 45.3 years of age. This was similar to the mean age at diagnosis of sporadic pheochromocytoma and notably older than in syndromic cases. Within families, age at onset ranged from 25 to 72 years. All tumors arose from the adrenal medulla, and about half of the patients had bilateral tumors. During follow-up of 4 to 16 years, there were no malignancies, defined by metastasis to nonchromaffin tissues, and no recurrences. In the original kindred (family 1), 7 sibs were affected with a total of 10 tumors. Four mutation carriers from this family remained without clinical disease at 43 to 58 years of age.

paragraphs.text: Toledo et al. (2015) studied a 6-generation family with a germline TMEM127 mutation. Of 151 individuals offered screening, 47 carried the mutation. Clinical data were available for 34 carriers, who were followed for 8.7 +/- 8.1 years (range, 1-20 years). Eleven carriers (32%) were diagnosed with pheochromocytoma at a median age of 43 years. Nine of these patients had symptoms beginning at a median of 29 years (range, 10-55 years), and 2 were asymptomatic. Tumors were multicentric in 5 patients (45%) and bilateral in 5 (45%). Six patients (54%) had at least 1 adrenomedullary nodule less than 10 mm across. No paragangliomas, distant metastases, or other manifestations were found. The youngest patient was diagnosed at 22 years of age, and the earliest symptoms were reported at age 10. The authors considered tumor multicentricity, nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia, and symptom onset more than a decade before diagnosis to be new findings in TMEM127-related pheochromocytoma.

paragraphs.text: Armaiz-Pena et al. (2021) reviewed 110 index patients with TMEM127 variants drawn from a registry, published reports, and public databases. Mean age was 45 years (range, 21-84 years), and females predominated (76 vs 34). Most patients had pheochromocytoma (94; 85.5%). Paraganglioma (10; 9%) and renal cell carcinoma (6; 5.4%) also occurred, either alone or together with pheochromocytoma. One-third of the patients had multiple tumors, 15.4% had a known family history, and 2.8% had metastatic pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma. Epinephrine alone or with norepinephrine made up 82% of the catecholamine profiles. The authors concluded that patients with TMEM127 variants often resemble those with sporadic nonmetastatic pheochromocytoma. They noted that paraganglioma and renal cell carcinoma may co-occur, but that a causal link required further evaluation.

paragraphs.text: Qin et al. (2010) sequenced genes in the FP locus using tumor DNA from the index case of the original family with familial pheochromocytoma (family 1). They identified a splice site mutation (IVS3-2A-C) in the TMEM127 gene. The mutation was present in the patient's germline DNA and in each of 6 other affected sibs, but not in 2 unaffected sibs.
